This overview explains the types of information Meridian may use to provide account access and banking features. The final policy should be completed by Meridian’s legal and privacy teams for the applicable operating entity and jurisdictions.
This can include your name, email address, profile details and information you enter when managing accounts, payment recipients, cards and security preferences.
Information may be used to create and maintain your account, provide requested features, authenticate sessions, process instructions, prevent misuse and respond to support requests.

Meridian uses technical and organisational measures intended to protect account information. No online service can guarantee absolute security; keep your sign-in details private and contact Meridian promptly if you suspect unauthorised access.
Essential session cookies and browser storage may be used to keep you signed in and support core website functions. See the Cookies page for more detail.
Information may be shared with service providers where needed to operate the service, or where disclosure is required by law. The final policy should identify relevant recipients and transfers.
Depending on where you live, you may have rights to access, correct, delete or restrict certain information. Contact Meridian through your account support channel to make a request.

Information is retained for as long as needed for the purposes described and applicable legal requirements. The final published policy should provide the controller identity, contact details, effective date and complaint route.
This notice may be updated as services and legal requirements change. The published version should show when it was last revised and how material changes are communicated.

These terms describe expected use of Meridian’s website and online banking services. They are a general draft and must be reviewed and completed for the operating entity and applicable jurisdiction before publication.

Use Meridian only for lawful purposes and in line with the instructions presented in your account. Keep your sign-in details confidential and tell Meridian if you believe someone else has accessed your account.
Check account, recipient and payment details before submitting an instruction. Some instructions may be difficult or impossible to cancel once processed.
Online services may occasionally be interrupted for maintenance, updates or events outside Meridian’s control. Any service commitments should be described in the final account terms.
Eligibility criteria, fees, interest rates, borrowing terms and product conditions vary by product and circumstance. Refer to the specific product documentation before applying or making a decision.
The Meridian name, design and website materials are protected by applicable intellectual property laws. Do not copy or misuse them without permission.
The final terms must explain responsibility, limitations, governing law and how to raise a complaint in a way that complies with local requirements.
The small things that keep the service working.
Meridian uses essential browser storage to support account access and core website functions. The final notice should be reviewed against the storage technologies enabled in each environment.
A session cookie helps the service recognise a signed-in session and maintain account access across requests.
A session token may also be held in browser local storage so the app can make authenticated requests in supported browser contexts.
This page describes storage used for essential service functions. If analytics, personalisation or advertising tools are added, this notice and any required consent controls must be updated.
You can clear cookies and local storage through your browser settings. Doing so may sign you out or prevent some account features from working.
The final policy should list the exact cookies and storage keys, their purpose, duration and any third-party providers, together with the correct contact and effective date.
